cues.en: It'll be a cold day in hell before I let twins fly long haul over water routes.
cues.zh: 要我允许双发飞机执飞跨洋远程航线，除非地狱冻成冰。

cues.en: Those were the words of Lynn Helms, administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration during the Reagan administration.
cues.zh: 这话出自 Lynn Helms，他是里根政府时期的美国联邦航空管理局局长。

cues.en: At the time, no commercial American airplane with two engines was allowed to fly anywhere farther than sixty minutes from a diversion airport.
cues.zh: 当时，美国的双发商用飞机一律不得飞离备降机场超过六十分钟航程。

cues.en: The belief was that, if one engine failed, the other could only safely fly the plane for about an hour, but this rule severely limited what smaller planes could do. On North Atlantic routes like New York to London, twin engine planes could only fly in these areas, but a direct route looked like this. The options were to either fly a twin engined plane on an inefficient routing or fly an inefficient three or four engine plane. There was no place for long and skinny routes between smaller cities using smaller planes since airlines couldn't legally fly those smaller planes. This one simple rule changed the very way airplanes were built. Now in the sixties, this sixty minute regulation only applied to planes with two engines.
cues.zh: 当时的看法是，如果一台发动机失效，另一台只能让飞机安全飞行约一小时，但这条规定严重限制了较小飞机能做什么。在像纽约到伦敦这样的北大西洋航线上，双发飞机只能在这些区域内飞行，而直飞航线看起来是这样的。选择要么让双发飞机走低效航线，要么飞一架低效的三发或四发飞机。用较小飞机在较小城市之间开通又长又窄的航线没有空间，因为航空公司不能合法飞那些较小飞机。这一条简单规定改变了飞机制造的方式。到了六十年代，这项六十分钟规定只适用于双发飞机。

cues.en: Of course, aircraft manufacturers could build quad engine jets, but those had to be huge for airlines to make their money's worth with the high fuel consumption. The seven forty seven's of the time could carry more than 400
cues.zh: 当然，飞机制造商可以造四发喷气客机，但受高油耗影响，这类飞机必须造得很大，航空公司才划算。当时的 747 可以搭载超过 400

cues.en: passengers.
cues.zh: 名乘客。

cues.en: They could therefore only fly on super high demand routes like New York to London to have any hope of being full. In order to start flying more convenient nonstop routes from smaller markets, planes had to get smaller while still being legally allowed to hop the pond. That's where trijets came into play. With three engines, these planes weren't subject to the same sixty minute regulation as twin jets. They could easily fly any Transatlantic route. That's why in the seventies and eighties, the long haul jets you'd see at airports were, for the most part, either seven forty seven's or tri jets like the d c 10. This sixty minute regulation was inconvenient
cues.zh: 因此，它们只能飞纽约到伦敦这种需求极高的航线，才有希望坐满。为了能从较小市场开通更方便的直飞航线，飞机必须变小，同时仍要合法跨越大西洋。三发客机因此登场。这些飞机有三台发动机，不受双发飞机那套 60 分钟规定的限制。它们可以轻松飞任何跨大西洋航线。所以在七八十年代，机场里看到的长途喷气客机大多要么是 747，要么是 DC-10 这样的三发客机。这项 60 分钟规定很不方便

cues.en: for Atlantic crossings, but in the Pacific, it actually changed how Hawaii as a state developed.
cues.zh: ……对跨大西洋飞行来说是这样，但在太平洋，它实际上改变了夏威夷作为一个州的发展轨迹。

cues.en: There are zero diversion airports between California and Hawaii, so the route isn't even close to covered under the sixty minute rule. As a result, airlines could only fly huge planes between the mainland and Hawaii,
cues.zh: California 和 Hawaii 之间没有任何备降机场，所以这条航线根本达不到“六十分钟规则”的要求。结果，航空公司只能在美国本土和 Hawaii 之间使用大型客机，

cues.en: which meant the planes could pretty much only fly to Honolulu.
cues.zh: 这意味着这些飞机基本只能飞往 Honolulu。

cues.en: There was virtually no service to the other islands from the mainland, which meant they were severely isolated.
cues.zh: 从美国本土到其他岛屿几乎没有任何航班，这意味着它们被严重孤立了。

cues.en: That's part of the reason why the tourism industry only picked up on the other islands in recent decades.
cues.zh: 这也是近几十年来旅游业只在其他岛屿发展起来的部分原因。

cues.en: The sixty minute rule originated from the days of piston driven propeller aircraft.
cues.zh: 六十分钟规则源自活塞驱动的螺旋桨飞机时代。

cues.en: With these, it was far more common for engines to just stop working mid flight. That's why there were contingency engines.
cues.zh: 那时候，发动机在飞行途中直接停转要常见得多。所以才有了应急发动机。

cues.en: The regulations just didn't adapt to the increased reliability of jet engines.
cues.zh: 监管规定只是没能跟上喷气发动机可靠性的提升。

cues.en: Statistically,
cues.zh: 从统计数据看，

cues.en: for every failure of a jet engine, there are a 117
cues.zh: 喷气发动机每出现一次故障，对应的就有 117 次

cues.en: piston engine failures.
cues.zh: 活塞发动机故障。

cues.en: Once the jet age rolled in, engine failure just wasn't as much of a concern. So in 1985,
cues.zh: 喷气机时代到来后，发动机故障就没那么令人担心了。于是在 1985 年，

cues.en: the FAA begrudgingly granted permission to Transworld Airlines to fly their twin engined seven sixty seven direct between Boston and Paris,
cues.zh: FAA 勉强批准 Transworld Airlines 用双发 767 在波士顿和巴黎之间直飞，

cues.en: a route taking it up to a hundred and twenty minutes away from diversion airports.
cues.zh: 这条航线会让飞机最远离备降机场达 120 分钟航程。

cues.en: This was the first example of a brand new FAA certification
cues.zh: 这是 FAA 一项全新认证的首个案例

cues.en: called ETOPS,
cues.zh: 名为 ETOPS，

cues.en: extended range twin engine operational performance standards, or more colloquially,
cues.zh: 即“增程双发运行性能标准”，或者更通俗地说，

cues.en: engines turn or passengers swim. Before an airline can fly a long over water route, they have to buy a plane with what's known as an ETOPS type rating. Basically, means that the plane was built with adequate redundancies,
cues.zh: 要么发动机转，要么乘客游泳。航空公司要飞长距离越洋航线，就必须购买带有所谓 ETOPS 型别等级的飞机。基本上，这意味着这架飞机在建造时具备足够的冗余、

cues.en: communication systems, and fire suppression systems to fly safely if one engine fails.
cues.zh: 通信系统和灭火系统，以便在一台发动机失效时仍能安全飞行。

cues.en: For example, the seven sixty seven, the first plane to get an ETOPS certification, has a type rating of a hundred and eighty minutes meaning it can fly anywhere as long as it's within a hundred and eighty minutes from a diversion airport. But just because a plane has an ETOPS type rating doesn't mean an airline can fly at ETOPS. They have to have a special maintenance plan, a special flight crew, special cabin crew, special dispatchers,
cues.zh: 例如，767 是首款获得 ETOPS 认证的飞机，其型别等级为 180 分钟，意味着只要距离备降机场不超过 180 分钟，它就能飞往任何地方。但飞机拥有 ETOPS 型别等级，并不意味着航空公司就能执行 ETOPS 运行。他们必须有专门的维护计划、专门的飞行机组、专门的客舱机组、专门的签派员、专门的燃油量，以及专门的旅客安置计划，因为仅仅有一条跑道，并不意味着飞机就能安全备降；而且飞机落地后，紧急情况也未必就结束了。

cues.en: special fuel quantities, and special passenger recovery plans since just because there's a runway doesn't mean a plane can safely divert since the emergency doesn't necessarily end once the plane lands.
cues.zh: 特殊燃油量，以及专门的乘客安置计划——因为有条跑道不代表飞机就能安全备降，而且紧急情况未必在飞机落地后就结束。

cues.en: Cold Bay, Alaska, for example, is a perfect diversion airport for routes between Asia and North America. It only has six commercial flights per week nowadays, but as a former air force base, it has an enormous runway. The only issue is that the town of Cold Bay has a population of a 108.
cues.zh: 比如阿拉斯加的冷湾，就是亚洲与北美之间航线的理想备降机场。如今它每周只有六班商业航班，但作为前空军基地，它拥有一条超长跑道。唯一的问题是，冷湾镇的人口只有108人。

cues.en: It's tiny, so any diversions automatically double or triple the amount of people in the small town. There certainly aren't enough hotel rooms or restaurants to house and feed stranded passengers.
cues.zh: 镇子太小了，任何一次备降都会让这个小镇的人口自动翻倍甚至变成三倍。这里的酒店房间和餐馆肯定不足以安置和供养滞留的乘客。

cues.en: So if airlines plan to use Cold Bay as a diversion airport, they need to make a plan for how to house, feed, and recover passengers within forty eight hours of landing. Last year, an American Airlines seven eighty seven was flying from Shanghai to Chicago when its right engine had an issue halfway across the Pacific Ocean. The plane quickly took a left turn diverting to Cold Bay. Even before landing, the passenger recovery plan was implemented as flight attendants served a second meal service early. Just a few hours after safely landing in Cold Bay, American's mechanics took off from Seattle bound for Cold Bay to start fixing the plane, while Alaska Airlines, American's partner, sent a seven thirty seven from Anchorage to pick up the stranded passengers. Meanwhile, flight attendants served the third set of meals they had stocked while waiting on the ground and the coast guard opened their heated hangar to passengers.
cues.zh:
所以，如果航空公司计划把 Cold Bay 作为备降机场，就需要制定计划，在落地后48小时内如何安置、供餐并转运旅客。
去年，美国航空一架787从上海飞往芝加哥，在太平洋中途右发动机出现问题。
飞机迅速左转，备降 Cold Bay。
甚至在落地前，旅客安置计划就已启动，乘务员提前提供了第二餐。
安全降落在 Cold Bay 仅几小时后，美国航空的机务就从西雅图起飞前往 Cold Bay 开始修飞机；同时，其合作伙伴阿拉斯加航空从安克雷奇派出一架737，接走滞留旅客。
与此同时，乘务员在地面等待时提供了储备的第三批餐食，海岸警卫队则向旅客开放了供暖机库。

cues.en: Just ten hours after the emergency landing, passengers were on their way to Anchorage where they spent the night before taking an American seven fifty seven to Chicago.
cues.zh: 紧急迫降仅十小时后，乘客们已在前往安克雷奇的路上；他们在那里过夜，随后搭乘美国航空757航班飞往芝加哥。

cues.en: That was a perfect example of how the passenger recovery plan worked.
cues.zh: 这完美体现了乘客恢复计划是如何奏效的。

cues.en: The quick response and defined plan helped the airline get passengers out safely and quickly. Now because of this solid engine reliability,
cues.zh: 快速响应和明确的计划帮助航空公司安全迅速地把乘客送离。现在，凭借过硬的发动机可靠性，

cues.en: numerous redundancies,
cues.zh: 大量冗余设计，

cues.en: and well designed passenger plans, airlines and airplanes can now receive some insane e top certifications.
cues.zh: 以及精心设计的乘客方案，航空公司和飞机现在可以获得一些非常厉害的ETOPS认证。

cues.en: The seven eighty seven Dreamliner,
cues.zh: 波音 787 梦想客机，

cues.en: the plane that diverted to Cold Bay, has a type rating of three hundred and thirty minutes. That means it can fly up to five and a half hours away from a diversion airport. Certain routes over long ocean stretches in the Southern Hemisphere were theoretically possible in the past with four engine planes, but were economically
cues.zh: 这架改降 Cold Bay 的飞机，型别等级为 330 分钟。这意味着它最多能飞到距备降机场 5.5 小时航程远的地方。过去，南半球长途跨洋的某些航线，用四发飞机理论上可行，但在经济上

cues.en: impossible since airlines could never fill the large planes on the low demand city pairs like Melbourne to Santiago.
cues.zh: 不可行，因为像墨尔本到圣地亚哥这类低需求城市对，航空公司永远无法坐满这些大型飞机。

cues.en: With the ETOPS three thirty certification,
cues.zh: 凭借 ETOPS 330 认证，

cues.en: LATAM Airlines can fly their small seven eighty seven economically
cues.zh: LATAM Airlines 就能让自家较小的 787 经济地

cues.en: on this relatively low demand route across the South Pacific. The Airbus a three fifty is even rated for ETOPS three seventy. It can fly six hours and ten minutes away from diversion airports. This plane can therefore fly everywhere on earth except directly over the South Pole. Because of this simple rule change, three and four engine planes are largely a relic of the past. Boeing and Airbus' largest jets are both their only four engine planes in production, the seven forty seven and a three eighty. Nearly all North Atlantic traffic today is on twin engine planes as smaller and smaller planes get e top certifications.
cues.zh: 执飞这条需求相对较低的南太平洋航线。Airbus A350 甚至获得了 ETOPS 370 认证。它能在距备降机场六小时十分钟的范围内飞行。因此，这架飞机可以飞遍地球，唯独不能直接飞越南极上空。由于这项简单的规则变更，三发和四发飞机基本上已成为历史。波音和空客最大的喷气机，都是各自唯一仍在生产的四发飞机：747 和 A380。如今，几乎所有北大西洋航班都由双发飞机执飞，因为越来越小的飞机也获得了 ETOPS 认证。

cues.en: Air Canada, for example, flies their tiny a 120 passenger a three nineteen with e top certification daily between St John's and London Heathrow. British Airways even sends the even smaller a three eighteen between New York and London City Airport.
cues.zh: 例如，加拿大航空每天用他们小巧的 120 座 A319（具备 ETOPS 认证）往返于圣约翰斯和伦敦希思罗之间。英国航空甚至派出更小的 A318 往返于纽约和伦敦城市机场之间。

cues.en: These routes would have been unimaginable
cues.zh: 这些航线在三十年前还难以想象

cues.en: thirty years ago, but the reliability of the airplanes of today mean that we need not fear flying small planes over big oceans.
cues.zh: 但如今飞机的可靠性意味着，我们不必害怕让小型飞机飞越大洋。
